note: 13 web fetch() calls with no backing route. Each is a live 404 and the page renders an empty state that reads as 'you have no data'. This list may only SHRINK. Two more were wrong paths and were fixed rather than baselined: /api/plaid/link-token was /api/financial/plaid/link-token, and /api/investments/signals/history was /signals/performance — always check for an existing route one directory over before building one.

why./api/financial/savings/auto-save <- src/: Correcting my own earlier note, which said this had no service behind it and was 'a feature to design'. That was wrong: public.savings_rules exists (user_id, goal_id, type, frequency, status, config, source/destination_account_id, total_saved). What actually blocks it is a SCOPE MISMATCH, not a missing table. AIGoalsOptimizer.tsx:86 POSTs {enabled} with NO goal id, and AIGoalsData.autoSaveEnabled (line 30) is one user-level boolean -- but savings_rules is per-goal, and goal-detail/[id]/page.tsx:30 renders autoSaveEnabled per goal. So 'enabled:true' has three readings with different behaviour: (a) set every one of the user's savings_rules to active, (b) store a new user-level preference column that new goals inherit, (c) materialise rules from the AI recommendations the optimizer just produced. My recommendation is (a): it needs no new column, and it makes the per-goal flag on goal-detail consistent -- a goal shows auto-save when it has an active rule. But (c) is a real reading given the component is an optimizer, and picking wrong means a button labelled 'Auto-save enabled!' silently creates or activates transfers of the user's money. That is an owner decision, not a default to guess.

verbMismatchWhy._what: The PATH resolves, so the resolve check passes; the handler does not export this METHOD, so Next.js answers 405 and the page swallows it. Shrink-only, like broken[]. HEAD and OPTIONS are exempt — Next.js derives HEAD from GET (verified: /api/health exports GET only and curl -I returned 200) and auto-implements OPTIONS.
verbMismatchWhy._pattern: THE VERB IS USUALLY THE FIRST THING WRONG, NOT THE ONLY THING. Two of these were checked against both sides and in both cases flipping the method alone would convert a visible 405 into a SILENT PARTIAL SAVE. Check the body shape against the handler before assuming a one-line fix. The same drift appears on mobile notification preferences — see mobile-app/scripts/api-calls-baseline.json.
verbMismatchWhy.PUT /api/financial/budgets/:id <- src/co: VERIFIED BOTH SIDES. Route exports PATCH, not PUT — but BudgetFormData sends {name, category, amount, period, alertThreshold, rolloverEnabled} while the PATCH handler destructures {name, budgetedAmount, period, rolloverEnabled, alertThreshold, isActive}. The client says amount, the server reads budgetedAmount, and category is not in the handler at all. Flipping to PATCH would save the name, period, threshold and rollover while silently discarding the AMOUNT — the one field a budget is about. Needs the field names reconciled in the same change.
Same route, same amount-vs-budgetedAmount drift as BudgetManagement.tsx. Fix both together.
verbMismatchWhy.POST /api/financial/budgets/adjust <- sr: The route exists but exports GET only; no write handler was ever written for adjusting a budget from a coach recommendation.
verbMismatchWhy.POST /api/investments/signals/generate <: No generate route exists. The call falls through to investments/signals/[id] with id="generate", which exports GET and PATCH. Same misnamed-sub-resource shape as the signals/history bug fixed earlier — check for an existing route under another name before building one.
verbMismatchWhy.POST /api/financial/budgets/apply-recomm: No apply-recommendation route. Falls through to budgets/[id] with id="apply-recommendation".
verbMismatchWhy.POST /api/chat/financial/sessions/:id/me: SENDING A MESSAGE in the financial chat. The route exports GET only, so the read path works and every send has always 405d. Highest user-visible impact in this list.
verbMismatchWhy.PATCH /api/chat/financial/sessions/:id <: Renaming a chat session. Route exports GET and DELETE; no update handler.
